subject: Performance sprint proposal: latency & streaming targets + costed options
body:
Message 1/4
From: Michael Jones <michael.jones@clearwave.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up on today's performance discussion

Thanks for the call today, Vivek — good overview of Redwood's serving options.

A few clarifying points from our side as we map requirements into procurement: 
- P95 latency target: ideally <=150ms for short responses (<=128 tokens) across US customers.
- Streaming behavior: our UI streams partial ASR-like updates; first-chunk latency matters (~<200ms to first token) and steady-state chunk latency target is ~<500ms for subsequent partials.
- Peak throughput: planning for 200 QPS with bursts to 350 for 60-90s.
- Concurrency: per-customer spikes up to 120 concurrent sessions, typical baseline ~20.
- Data residency: US only, no shared KV across customers.

Can you confirm which levers you'd recommend to reach these SLOs with a cost estimate range (monthly) for a production-ready config? Also, what model variants you'd suggest (quantized vs fp16, distillation) for conversational latency without severe quality drop?

Attachments: clearwave_perf_req.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Jones
Head of Product Ops, ClearWave Retail

---

Message 2/4
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Michael Jones <michael.jones@clearwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on today's performance discussion

Hi Michael — appreciated the clear run-through. Re: your bullets: here's a concise readout of recommended levers and our next-step ask so we can produce a firm costed proposal.

Summary recommendations (initial):
- Latency (P95 <=150ms): prioritize smaller context windows, continuous batching tuned to 80ms max, and a low-latency execution kernel. Suggest model variant: 6B quantized int8 for most traffic, 13B fp16 for high-quality fallbacks.
- Streaming first-token: ensure warm prefix caching and short path for token generation (pre-warm KV cache with 50ms TTL for active sessions).
- Throughput & bursts: dedicated pool with autoscale headroom + burst capacity (predictable node count to handle 350 QPS short bursts).
- Concurrency: soft-shard sessions across pools and use per-session KV caching to avoid repeated prompt costs.
- Cost levers: continuous batching (adaptive), prefix caching, per-route quantization profiles, and model-routing policy (cheap variant for majority; fallback to larger models for 5-10% of requests).

Estimated monthly range (very preliminary):
- Baseline (200 QPS sustained, 20 concurrent baseline): $32k - $45k/mo (quantized-first variant + caching).
- Production w/ burst headroom & higher-quality fallback (350 QPS bursts, 120 concurrent spikes): $60k - $90k/mo (dedicated capacity + higher instance mix).

What we need from you to firm these numbers:
1) representative prompt/response size distribution (median/95th in tokens)
2) % of queries that must hit high-quality model vs acceptable on quantized model (ballpark)
3) any hard SLOs for first-token time for streaming UI vs aggregate P95

If helpful I can loop in Rishi for kernel/quantization tradeoffs and Ben for batching/autoscale mechanics. Proposed next step: a short technical spike (3 days) to run a producer/consumer replay against a test harness and come back with validated latency/throughput curves and a line-item cost model.

Are you available for a 30-minute sync next week to confirm data and greenlight the spike?

Best,
Vivek
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: cleared for reference: clearwave_perf_req.pdf

Message 3/4 (internal)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance spike proposal — cost mechanics and ops plan

Vivek/Laura — quick technical readout. I ran a back-of-envelope on their targets with assumptions: avg response 60 tokens, 95th 120 tokens.

Findings / options:
- Option A (cost-optimized): All traffic routed to int8-quantized 6B + prefix caching + continuous batching. Expect P95 around 120-160ms depending on batching window; good for 85-90% of requests. Monthly infra est: ~$28k-$38k.
- Option B (hybrid): Quantized 6B primary, 13B fp16 fallback for 5-10% of sessions routed by quality gate. Keep tight batching (<=50ms). P95 for primary ~110-140ms; for fallback ~180-240ms. Monthly: ~$45k-$65k.
- Option C (quality-first): Majority on 13B fp16 with aggressive caching and larger dedicated pool. P95 ~140-200ms but higher tail on bursts; Monthly: ~$80k-$115k.

Operational notes:
- Continuous batching helps amortize cost but increases P95 if target windows are >80ms — we should do adaptive batching capped at 60ms for this customer.
- For streaming first-token constraint, pre-warm strategy + a tiny headroom of low-latency instances (fp16) dedicated to initial token emission works well.
- Quantization validation: need Rishi to run quality regression on 1k critical prompts sample (customer to provide).

Action items I recommend before the spike:
- Ask ClearWave for token distribution (Vivek to request)
- Run quick 1k prompt quality check vs quantized 6B and 13B fp16 (Rishi)
- Prepare test harness with synthetic burst pattern (Ben)

I can scope infra for the 3-day spike and produce latency buckets and cost per 1k tokens outputs.

—Ben
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: clearwave_model_options_costs.csv (CSV, 12KB)

Message 4/4
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Michael Jones <michael.jones@clearwave.com>, Sara Cole <sara.cole@clearwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on today's performance discussion — proposed 3-day spike and next steps

Hi Michael / Sara — thanks again for the call and the perf doc. Based on your targets we propose the following next steps: 

1) 3-day technical spike (goal: validate SLOs & provide line-item cost model) — scope:
   - Replays against synthetic burst profile matching your expected peaks (200 QPS baseline, 350 QPS bursts).
   - Quantization regression: run 1k focused prompts to compare int8 6B vs 13B fp16 quality.
   - Latency profiling: measure P50/P95/P99 across batching windows (20/40/60ms) and streaming-first-token times.

2) Deliverables after spike (3 business days):
   - Latency/throughput curves, cost estimates by option (Option A/B/C), recommended quantization profile and routing policy.
   - Recommended config for production (autoscale + burst headroom, caching TTLs, per-route quantization).

3) Timeline & approvals:
   - Spike start: pending your go-ahead and data (prompt samples + token distribution).
   - Cost to run spike (one-time, covered by Redwood for this qualifying PoC): $0 — Redwood will cover infra for spike.

4) Asks from ClearWave to proceed:
   - 1k sample prompts (anonymized) with expected response length distribution
   - Confirmation of strict first-token streaming SLO (if <200ms is required, we’ll prioritize a small warm headroom pool)

Would you be available Thursday 5/20 10:00-10:30am PT for a short sync to hand off the artifacts and confirm the prompt sample? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and the small NDA addendum (if legal needs it).

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123
